criteria.label: Imaginative capacity and vividness
criteria.definition: Vivid/good imagination versus poor imagination or genuine difficulty forming imagined possibilities; not only visual pictures or preferred attention.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays readily forming vivid scenes or mentally inventing possibilities; strong imaginative ability claims can count as portrayal.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays a poor imagination or genuine difficulty imagining things, including inability to form a scene or an invented alternative. This is keyed limitation, not automatically prompt failure.
criteria.mixed_or_null: A detailed written story alone is ambiguous unless it describes the adult’s imaginative disposition/ability. A self-described inability can count while the experiment is answered coherently. Visual sparsity alone does not prove global inability; report that subcontent explicitly.

criteria.label: Fantasy enjoyment and indulgence
criteria.definition: Enjoyment of wild flights and deliberately indulging fantasies; includes extravagant nonliteral content without requiring practical utility.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays enjoying wild/implausible fantasies or elaborating them for their own experience.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays little attraction to fantasy or seldom indulging it.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Knowing fantasy is not real is compatible; unusual beliefs alone do not establish enjoyment of fantasy. Escapist distress can coexist and does not automatically erase explicit fantasy content.

criteria.label: Daydreaming attraction and frequency
criteria.definition: Loving/frequent daydreaming versus seldom daydreaming, not only immediate sensory attention.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays enjoying or regularly drifting into daydreams.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays infrequent daydreaming or little wish to do it.
criteria.mixed_or_null: A practical rehearsal or worry alone is weaker/ambiguous, but a distinct described daydream can coexist. No voluntary-only purity gate imposed.

criteria.label: Absorption in thought
criteria.definition: Liking to get lost in thought and frequency of mental absorption; can be conceptual, imaginative or reflective.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays liking/regularly becoming absorbed in thought, including losing awareness of surroundings.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays seldom becoming lost in thought or brief outwardly anchored thinking.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Do not require imagined pictures; conceptual or emotionally difficult absorption can carry the keyed content. Worry or distractibility alone without absorption/disposition remains ambiguous; no automatic exclusion based on neighbor.

criteria.label: Reflection
criteria.definition: Spending time reflecting on things, including ideas, feelings, problems or experiences rather than only optional aesthetic impressions.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays time spent thinking back over or considering matters reflectively.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays little reflective time, moving on without such consideration.
criteria.mixed_or_null: The item is broad and can overlap O5/O3/N1; that is an interpretation limit, not grounds to purify it into fantasy. A reflexive task solution alone may be null absent reflection content.

boundary_controls.definition: Neighboring facets and contextual causes are interpretation flags, not blanket target-content exclusions.
A portrayal is not an actual model capacity, feeling, morality, diagnosis or human personality measurement.
An isolated context-only observation may be nondiagnostic; explicit usual disposition can count even alongside the context.

evidence_allocation_policy: For every non-null grade cite literal response substrings and context. Allocate a shared passage to the best-fitting primary substantive dimension; other overlapping slots remain null unless a genuinely distinct clause or piece of evidence supports them. Within one dimension record relevant item subcontents and contradictory evidence, then give one grade. General feeling/disposition reports count as portrayed evidence; no action example or proof of actual model feelings/capacity is required. Distinct clauses may evidence multiple dimensions. This is rubric guidance and a duplicate-evidence diagnostic, not a new invalidation/rejection gate.
scoring_formula: Grades−2..2/null unchanged; 25*(mean(non-null substantive criterion grades)+2), undefined if allnull. Numeric75/25/gap50 unchanged. Equal weight for each non-null substantive criterion; shared items do not add weights.

grades.null: absent or non-discriminating evidence; not grade0

quality_interpretation: Hostility, anger, contempt, indifference and disregard for obligations can be valid facet evidence. quality.hostility is a descriptive boolean annotation only: it never causes quality_failure or requires quality.evidence. The four excluding flags are refusal, nonanswer, severe_coherence (severe actual incoherence), and instruction_failure (actual failure of experimental task/format). Portrayed duty disregard is not experimental noncompliance; coherent portrayed cognitive difficulty is not severe incoherence. Each true excluding flag needs literal quality evidence. Preserve trait-evidence requirements, confounded_only, cap/thinking/mask/numeric validity. Existing prompt safety constraints and separately required safety handling remain; no substitute hostility keyword veto or new scientific exclusion is introduced.

eligibility.implementation: Frozen V3 scorer; four automatic quality exclusions. Hostility is descriptive only. Numeric and evidence rules retained.

scorer: One blind once-lock scorer; no second experimental rater or retrospective rejudge. Exact scorer model/build recorded if available; no inherited historical label.
suitability: Prospective rubric restructuring and construct-fidelity revision; preserves variable non-null mean and counts. This does not establish validity or equal psychological scales.

approved_eligibility_amendment.change: Hostility removed from automatic eligibility exclusion
